leads.summary: Accessible checkbox fix depends on a Quickshell accessibility bridge not shipped in 0.3.1
leads.consequence: The new onToggleAction correctly handles direct QML action calls, but screen readers cannot discover or invoke it on the installed quickshell 0.3.1-1. Upstream fixed missing accessibility information in commit 916a0dd after v0.3.1, by removing the initial QCoreApplication destroyed before constructing the GUI application. The fixture invokes Accessible.toggleAction directly and cannot establish an assistive technology path. Upgrading/patching Quickshell to contain that fix (and testing the tree) is needed before presenting this as an accessible end-user control; normal pointer and o shortcut work.
leads.triage: confirmed by coordinator (factual), used as qualifier; quickshell 916a0dd is 7 commits after v0.3.1; #13212 docs state releases up to 0.3.1 publish no accessibility tree; Omarchy installs Arch quickshell 0.3.1-1. Published in earlier-findings details.

leads.summary: Open UI accessibility PR #13212 and this PR install two action handlers on the same switch
leads.consequence: When #13212's base ToggleSwitch gets an accessibility toggle/press action, it calls toggled(), which calls this instance's onToggled. This instance also handles the very same Accessible action directly. A single QML Accessible.toggleAction activates both handlers. In a minimal Qt fixture with synchronous setting updates, one action causes two changes and returns the option to its initial false value. The real shell updates live widget settings inline during updateEntryInline; integrate these PRs by dropping instance action handlers and setting the new accessibleName while retaining onToggled.
leads.triage: confirmed by Opus follow-up, published as NEW-2; Opus harness: Toggle 2 calls and Press 2 calls with #13212+332414d; fix verified.

leads.summary: Opting into offline peers also reveals Tailscale sharee/ingress nodes that status intentionally hides
leads.consequence: ShareeNode is an upstream status field for nodes owned by users shared to us, including ingress/relay peers; these are not tailnet machines one can act on. With Online:false they remain invisible under the default setting, but this PR includes every offline Peer when showOfflinePeers=true, regardless of ShareeNode. A synthetic upstream-shaped status shows funnel-ingress-node alongside a real offline laptop. Open PR #6471 adds a ShareeNode filter, but its tailscale-test.sh expectation conflicts with this PR's offline rows, so coordinate the filter and expected output when merging.

leads.summary: Open #7623's virtualized peer list conflicts with the newly cached offline-peer service and Machines header
leads.consequence: #7623 changes the peer publishing and panel list to avoid rebuilding thousands of QML delegates on every poll. Combining its own diff with this head using its actual base leaves two Service conflicts, at the reset and publish paths, plus two Panel conflicts at the Machines header and peer row. Picking one side alone either drops this PR's offline switch or #7623's peer cache/virtualization, and mapping #7623's publishPeers to the now readonly public peers instead of _peers cannot update the model. Integrate _peers with change-detected publishing and the virtualized row, including the offline toggle and both test suites, before merging both. No merged QML fixture was run because the files have unresolved conflict markers.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (R1-F5); corroboration of #7623 conflict hunks

leads.summary: Open #10510's test conflicts with this PR's machine-name assertions and its source guard becomes misleading
leads.consequence: #10510 changes only exit-node labels to MagicDNS and explicitly guards that machine rows keep friendly OS hostnames. This PR changes Model.displayHostName and hence DisplayName for machine rows to the first DNS label while leaving the PeerRow source expression unchanged. After the two code changes merge, #10510's regex guard for the unchanged PeerRow expression still passes despite no longer verifying its claimed OS-host behavior. The two additions to tailscale-test.sh also conflict: reconcile the test expectations and drop/rewrite the now invalid guard before considering both merged. The code-side Model/Panel/Service merge-file results have no markers, but the test has one conflict hunk.
leads.triage: partly in Opus final (R1-F4); regex point dropped; claim about #10510's own test belongs to that PR

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The runtime fixture fails on current `quattro`, and #13212 would double-toggle the offline switch.

At `332414d`, the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13248#issuecomment-5854947593)'s Toggle and manual points are **resolved**; open-PR notes stand.

<details><summary>Details on the earlier findings</summary>

Verification only, not a defect. It drives Qt's own accessibility action dispatch (`QAccessibleInterface::actionInterface()->doAction(...)`, which is where an AT-SPI DoAction request ends up) on a minimal QML stand-in for the offline switch. The stand-in has the same declarations as `Panel.qml` L705-715: a plain `Item` with a declared `checked` property bound to the saved state, `Accessible.role: Accessible.CheckBox`, `Accessible.checked: checked`, and the Press and Toggle handlers. `switch-prev.qml` is the same file without `Accessible.onToggleAction` (as at 489beac). No assistive technology or D-Bus is involved.

`switch-head.qml`:

```qml
import QtQuick

Window {
  id: win
  width: 200; height: 100
  visible: true
  property bool shown: false
  property int writes: 0
  function toggleOfflinePeers() { writes++; shown = !shown }

  component FakeToggleSwitch: Item {
    property bool checked: false
    signal toggled()
  }

  FakeToggleSwitch {
    id: offlineSwitch
    objectName: "offlineSwitch"
    width: 40; height: 20
    checked: win.shown
    Accessible.role: Accessible.CheckBox
    Accessible.name: "Show offline peers"
    Accessible.checked: checked
    Accessible.onPressAction: win.toggleOfflinePeers()
    Accessible.onToggleAction: win.toggleOfflinePeers()
    onToggled: win.toggleOfflinePeers()
  }
}
```

`main.cpp` (build: `g++ -std=c++17 -fPIC -o harness main.cpp $(pkg-config --cflags --libs Qt6Quick Qt6Qml Qt6Gui Qt6Core)`; run: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen ./harness switch-head.qml toggle`):

```cpp
#include <QGuiApplication>
#include <QQmlApplicationEngine>
#include <QAccessible>
#include <QQuickItem>
#include <cstdio>

static void report(const char *label, QObject *win, QQuickItem *sw, QAccessibleInterface *iface)
{
    std::printf("%s: writes=%d shown=%s checked=%s a11yChecked=%s\n", label,
                win->property("writes").toInt(),
                win->property("shown").toBool() ? "true" : "false",
                sw->property("checked").toBool() ? "true" : "false",
                iface->state().checked ? "true" : "false");
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    QGuiApplication app(argc, argv);
    QQmlApplicationEngine engine;
    engine.load(QUrl::fromLocalFile(QString::fromLocal8Bit(argv[1])));
    if (engine.rootObjects().isEmpty()) { std::printf("load failed\n"); return 2; }
    QObject *win = engine.rootObjects().first();
    QQuickItem *sw = win->findChild<QQuickItem *>("offlineSwitch");
    if (!sw) { std::printf("switch missing\n"); return 3; }
    QAccessibleInterface *iface = QAccessible::queryAccessibleInterface(sw);
    if (!iface) { std::printf("no accessible interface\n"); return 4; }
    QAccessibleActionInterface *act = iface->actionInterface();
    if (!act) { std::printf("no action interface\n"); return 5; }
    std::printf("qt=%s role=%d (CheckBox=%d) actions=[%s]\n", qVersion(), int(iface->role()),
                int(QAccessible::CheckBox), qPrintable(act->actionNames().join(", ")));
    report("initial", win, sw, iface);
    const QString which = QString::fromLocal8Bit(argv[2]);
    const QString action = which == "press" ? QAccessibleActionInterface::pressAction()
                                            : QAccessibleActionInterface::toggleAction();
    for (int i = 1; i <= 2; ++i) {
        act->doAction(action);
        app.processEvents();
        report(qPrintable(QString("after %1 #%2").arg(action).arg(i)), win, sw, iface);
    }
    win->setProperty("shown", !win->property("shown").toBool());
    app.processEvents();
    report("after flipping saved state directly", win, sw, iface);
    return 0;
}
```

Output, Qt 6.11.2. Without `Accessible.onToggleAction` (489beac), Toggle:

```text
qt=6.11.2 role=44 (CheckBox=44) actions=[Toggle, Press, SetFocus, Press]
initial: writes=0 shown=false checked=false a11yChecked=false
after Toggle #1: writes=0 shown=false checked=true a11yChecked=true
after Toggle #2: writes=0 shown=false checked=false a11yChecked=false
after flipping saved state directly: writes=0 shown=true checked=true a11yChecked=true
```

With `Accessible.onToggleAction` (332414d), Toggle:

```text
qt=6.11.2 role=44 (CheckBox=44) actions=[Toggle, Press, SetFocus, Press, Toggle]
initial: writes=0 shown=false checked=false a11yChecked=false
after Toggle #1: writes=1 shown=true checked=true a11yChecked=true
after Toggle #2: writes=2 shown=false checked=false a11yChecked=false
after flipping saved state directly: writes=2 shown=true checked=true a11yChecked=true
```

Press gives `writes=1`, then `writes=2`, with `shown` and `checked` in step in both variants.

- Omarchy ships Quickshell 0.3.1. [#13212](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13212) notes that releases up to 0.3.1 publish no accessibility tree for any window, which upstream commit `916a0dd` fixes. Screen readers reach this switch, and the earlier Impact applies, only with a Quickshell build that includes it.
</details>

### Fixture fails on `quattro`

#13450 added a `modifiers` argument to `PanelKeyCatcher.textKey`, so the fixture's `textKey("O")` (line 91) throws. Rebased, the runtime test times out.

**Suggested change:** use `textKey("O", 0)`; it passes on both bases.

<details><summary>Reproducer (current quattro)</summary>

Current `quattro` changed `PanelKeyCatcher`'s signal to `textKey(string text, int modifiers)` in 349ecc09 (#13450). A JavaScript call to that signal with only the text now throws `Error: Insufficient arguments`, which is what `panel.testKeys.textKey("O")` at `test/shell.d/fixtures/tailscale-peers/shell.qml:91` does.

Minimal check from a checkout of current `quattro` (e332dc9), with no compositor needed:

```bash
ln -s "$repo/shell/Commons" "$stage/Commons"
```

Output on `quattro` e332dc9 (Quickshell 0.3.1, Qt 6.11.2):

```text

 DEBUG qml: two-argument call ok
```

Output with the PR's head 332414d (its `shell/Ui` and `shell/Commons` are unchanged from base d201fb9), for comparison:

```text

  WARN: expression for onTriggered@qs:@/qs/shell.qml:15

```

The PR's own peer fixture, on `quattro` e332dc9 merged with 332414d (run under Qt's offscreen platform with `KeyboardPanel` replaced by a plain `Item` stand-in, not under Wayland), stops at line 91 and never prints a RESULT line. `quickshell` is then killed by the test script's `timeout 20` (exit 124):

With line 91 changed to `panel.testKeys.textKey("O", 0)`, the same fixture prints `RESULT pass` both on the merged tree and on 332414d alone (on 332414d it also logs `Too many arguments, ignoring 1`, which the runtime test's error pattern does not match).
</details>

### Double toggle with #13212

With #13212, `ToggleSwitch` emits `toggled()` on Toggle and Press. The switch keeps its handlers, so one action calls `toggleOfflinePeers()` twice and the second undoes the first.

**Suggested change:** in whichever PR lands second, use `accessibleName: "Show offline peers"` instead of the switch's `Accessible.*` lines.

<details><summary>Reproducer (quattro + #13212 + this PR)</summary>

With #13212 (3ace0a2) and this PR (332414d) both merged onto `quattro` (e332dc9), one accessibility action on the **Show offline peers** switch calls `toggleOfflinePeers()` twice. The merge has no textual conflict.

- #13212 gives `ToggleSwitch` its own handlers: `Accessible.onToggleAction` and `Accessible.onPressAction` emit `toggled()`.
- The switch in `Panel.qml` still declares `Accessible.onToggleAction` and `Accessible.onPressAction` as well as `onToggled`.
- QML connects handlers declared by the component and by its user on the same attached object side by side, so both run.

```bash
git fetch origin quattro pull/13212/head:pr-13212 pull/13248/head:pr-13248
git checkout --detach origin/quattro
git merge --no-edit pr-13212
git merge --no-edit pr-13248
# current quattro needs the modifiers argument (PanelKeyCatcher.textKey, #13450)
sed -i 's/    panel.testKeys.textKey("O")$/    panel.testKeys.textKey("O", 0)/' test/shell.d/fixtures/tailscale-peers/shell.qml
bash test/shell.d/tailscale-peers-runtime-test.sh
bash test/shell.d/ui-accessibility-test.sh
```

The PR's runtime fixture on that tree ran under Qt's offscreen platform with `KeyboardPanel` replaced by a plain `Item` stand-in, not under Wayland. It reports:

```text

 DEBUG qml: RESULT failed
```

#13212's name check (runs without a compositor):

```text
Unnamed first-party controls:
  shell/plugins/panels/tailscale/Panel.qml:708 ToggleSwitch
```

A review-only copy of the fixture emits each input once and logs every settings write. The settings mock applies each write synchronously, as the shell's in-place inline-settings update does. Output on the same tree:

```text

 DEBUG qml: WRITE 1 showOfflinePeers=true
 DEBUG qml: WRITE 2 showOfflinePeers=false
 DEBUG qml: STATE after one accessible Toggle: calls=2 saved=false switch=false peers=1
```

On the same merge, replacing the switch's five `Accessible.*` lines with `accessibleName: "Show offline peers"` (keeping `onToggled`) gives these results:

</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

Screen readers reach the switch only with a Quickshell build that includes upstream commit `916a0dd` (see the earlier-findings details). A click and the `o` key call `toggleOfflinePeers()` once. The net-unchanged result assumes the shell applies each settings write immediately, as its source does; with a deferred update the switch would flip once, with a redundant write.
</details>
